where-the-river-begins.rationale: Naturalistic, rough-edged drama about migration cast with non-professional Indigenous performers, dealing with displacement and paramilitary violence, though pitched more lyrically and tenderly than a tense thriller

the-daughters-of-abraham.rationale: A first feature in French, played realistically, following a Muslim woman and a Jewish woman whose renewed friendship is upended by a sudden death; it looks hard at religion and gender but stays a close, small-scale drama.

nobodys-violence.rationale: Wavelengths hosts Cote's dystopian film about a euthanasia facilitator, 148 minutes in French, which keeps changing form from science-fiction fable to conspiracy thriller to comedy in Bunuel's vein, driven throughout by an unsettled energy

re-pair.rationale: A documentary built from talk: 19 duos of Black and Jewish public figures speaking frankly, warmly and with jokes, across 131 minutes about antisemitism and the Israel/Palestine divide.

blindspot-berlin.rationale: A gripping police-investigation drama that pieces together the run-up to the 2016 Breitscheidplatz attack, holding nothing back as it digs into wiretaps, informants and radicalization, in German, Arabic and Turkish.

in-waves.rationale: An English-language animated adaptation of a graphic novel dealing with cancer and bereavement, tender and slow-moving, treating the ocean as sacred, with a distinctive look built from combined 2D and 3D techniques.

smudge-the-blades.rationale: An underdog hockey comedy-drama following the Bad News Bears template, tougher and heavier in tone, with fast-paced on-ice action and jokes, unfolding on a reserve in Northern Alberta.

love-is-the-monster.rationale: A daring dystopia set in the tropics, part kidnapping thriller and part genre exercise, building dread around class division, with Paulina Garcia leading a Spanish-language cast.

pretenders.rationale: A standard-format music documentary built from interviews and archive footage about Chrissie Hynde, hard-edged and sharply dressed, with exciting live clips and a death shaping its middle section.

at-night.rationale: Beatrice Gibson's first feature in Wavelengths, shot on 16mm, works as collective autofiction in a poetic register rather than conventional storytelling, sliding among fiction, documentary, and dream in several languages, with a sombre mood

darlene-love-i-know-where-ive-been.rationale: A standard interview-driven music documentary, upbeat and affectionate in tone, mixing testimony with performance footage and well-known songs, though it stretches to a lengthy 145 minutes.

in-conversation-with-andrew-scott.rationale: An onstage interview with Andrew Scott covering the breadth of roles across his career; a nonfiction talk rather than a film with a story.

the-bovine-with-the-curved-horns.rationale: A boy's perspective on paramilitary violence in the Ciénaga Grande, told through Caribbean fantasy and magical realism, acted by locals, blending folklore with everyday rhythm in finely graded black-and-white.

a-good-little-soldier.rationale: A work of French social realism about how capitalist systems strip people of humanity and leave them isolated, told in familiar formal terms and driven by intense turns from Rohrwacher and Lindon.

the-secret-lives-of-baba-segis-wives.rationale: A Nollywood drama of a polygamous household, witty and cutting by turns, moving among the wives' viewpoints and using comedy to lay bare the damage of childlessness and sexual coercion over 149 minutes

in-the-heart-of-the-south.rationale: A tense psychological thriller about a double who worms her way in, moving fast and with humour and style, while taking aim at how Toronto's art scene handles Indigenous artists

oxygen-masks-will-not-drop-automatically.rationale: Set in 1980s Brazil, this Portuguese-language drama runs 140 minutes and tells a conventional story of the AIDS years, its bright nightclub world running alongside shame and mortality, pleasure and fear inseparable

minotaur.rationale: Zvyagintsev took the Cannes Grand Prix with this 171-minute study of a manager filling draft quotas, shot coldly by Mikhail Krichman, its ethical decay sliding into thriller territory once he kills.

strong-son-2.rationale: Ian Bawa's first feature follows a bodybuilder sunk in worry and self-doubt while looking after his father, breaking down in tears in public, set within a Sikh family; mostly English with some Punjabi.

silenced-nights.rationale: A grim drama about drug-war shootings in Manila, filmed in vérité style on location in the Happyland slum, following an inquiry that runs into one dead end after another.

rehearsals-for-a-revolution.rationale: A first-person essay film that digs into personal recollection using family footage and broadcast news, structured in five chapters tracing Iran's political wounds; took the L'\u0152il d'Or at Cannes.

eklipse.rationale: A lyrically realist story of growing up in the Austrian countryside in 1999, in German, mixing home-video tape into the fiction, with the concealed truth of a father's sickness giving it a subdued weight.

furies.rationale: Set against Lebanon's frozen banking system, this 164-minute Arabic-language robbery thriller in Beirut runs on quick cutting and a tense countdown as its characters chase time they cannot afford to lose.

river.rationale: Bold, tense first feature in slasher mode: a blank-faced stalker in the mould of the Shape, stripped-down suspense, and rural dreamlike unease closing in on a family stranded on open water.

all-of-a-sudden.rationale: Hamaguchi's 226-minute talk-driven work, structured around long conversations on sickness and looking after others, filmed inside an operating care home with actual residents, in French and Japanese

arrested-memory.rationale: SABU works in comic genre pastiche here: overlapping pursuits, musical numbers, inept police and gangsters, staged as fast Mandarin-Japanese action comedy shadowed by guilt and a detective losing his memory.

kick-on.rationale: A savage siege thriller built on extreme violence and full-body gore in the vein of Green Room, with dread wound tight across one night in Melbourne.

le-faux-soir.rationale: Roskam, who made Bullhead, directs a brisk and enjoyable thriller about wartime resistance that moves with the speed and flair of a heist picture; in French, running 163 minutes.

angh.rationale: Theja Rio's first feature, shot on 16mm in Konyak, sits close to a father and son while watching missionary conversion without sentiment, unhurried across 133 minutes and carried by a sound design built on space.

seventeen.rationale: Naturalist drama unfolding across 17 hours as three queer Indigenous sex workers race personal deadlines in a rough part of central Vancouver; weighty and formally familiar, largely in English with some Cree.

spring-in-a-small-town.rationale: Fei Mu's 1948 lyrical romance about desire held in check, built from extended shots, deliberate compositions and expressive light, screening in a new 4K restoration of a film long placed in the Chinese canon

intermission.rationale: A 255-minute memoir in montage drawing on Yonfan's 15 features, sitting outside both documentary and the usual essay-about-cinema form, assembled more like a music anthology, with editing that loops back on itself with great skill

trash-mountain.rationale: A witty, perceptive film about returning home, mixing disrespectful humour with warmth; familiar indie dramedy shape, but with genuine mourning running beneath it.

a-long-winter.rationale: A 147-minute drama of family grief in which Haigh's unhurried, close-in direction meets Toibin's restrained narration, loading each pause, look and small movement with meaning.

our-loves.rationale: A 147-minute film in Hebrew and Arabic built from linked storylines, each carrying its own private sorrow, until disaster pushes the characters into collective survival; its power lies in feeling and depth rather than momentum.

my-wife-cries.rationale: A German-language work of slow, contemplative art cinema: Schanelec shoots on 35mm in a grave, stripped-down key, building a lament of estrangement and hurt from framings like still-life paintings, broken by odd interruptions.

tehran-under-the-skin.rationale: A fly-on-the-wall Persian-language documentary set inside the practices of two Tehran plastic surgeons, inquisitive and warm and often funny, with restrained, composed surgery scenes and the country's political violence felt at the edges.

how-we-stand.rationale: A gripping story of three sisters whose lives bear the mark of Indigenous relocation programs, carrying trauma and sexual violence yet buoyed by magic-realist touches and comic jabs at the Hollywood western

diary-of-a-mad-old-man.rationale: A finely tuned interior drama, running 145 minutes in Japanese and Mandarin, about coded gestures and unruly wanting between a stroke-paralyzed widower and the daughter-in-law who nurses him

the-unknown.rationale: A brooding, dread-soaked riddle of swapped bodies and shifting selves, this 170-minute Cannes Competition standout twists into maze-like unease, drawing Lynch and De Palma parallels and carrying a bleak undertow

stuffed.rationale: A warped song-filled black comedy about taxidermy and yearning, cheerfully ghoulish and pitched high, starring Jodie Comer, at 147 minutes a lengthy sit in a premium premiere slot.

bitter-christmas.rationale: Almod\u00f3var nests tales inside tales like facing mirrors, mixing dark thriller shading, soap-opera reversals, and rich colour to look at mourning, love, and how far artists may go with other people's lives

back-in-black.rationale: Sharp-toothed dark comedy: Walken is a foul-tongued mortician whose granddaughter engineers deadly accidents to bring business to the family funeral parlour, told plainly with big laughs and only a light macabre streak

cheyenne.rationale: A standard-shape sports documentary tracking four women bronc riders, mixing high-energy arena footage with calmer scenes of friendship, histories of trauma, and the unequal treatment women face in the sport.

still-night-burning-house.rationale: A first-person documentary about an uncle who took his own life, striking to look at and emotionally direct, following a family's slow grieving between Toronto and Vietnam.

we-are-all-strangers.rationale: Running 187 minutes, Anthony Chen ends his Growing Up trilogy with an unhurried, humane portrait of a makeshift family, its aches and maturing, and the class rifts around them, mostly spoken in Mandarin

half.rationale: Indian frontier Western crossed with vampire horror, staged by the fight choreographer of The Raid 2, sending twin revenants on a bloody revenge rampage through Rajasthan across several Indian languages.

once-upon-a-time-in-harlem.rationale: Harlem Renaissance figures gathered at a 1972 party, filmed with several 16mm cameras and left loose and talk-driven, the exchanges by turns funny, impassioned, and touched with sadness, preserving that movement as it lived

onwards-and-sideways.rationale: A familiar British sickness comedy-drama mixing grief, jokes, and slowly earned intimacy; it treats degenerative illness plainly while letting cheeky humour lighten it, running an easy 140 minutes suited to a Gala slot

voices.rationale: A 1967 Detroit story confined to one motel room, dark in the manner of crime cinema and centred on a scam born of desperation, its catchy song sequences opening up the grim tale of fame's corruption.

soumsoum-the-night-of-the-stars.rationale: Set on Chad's Ennedi plateau, Haroun follows a girl shunned for her second sight, grounding fantasy in realism; slow and myth-inflected, spoken in Arabic and French, weighted toward banishment and the dead

the-assassins.rationale: At 161 minutes, this broad-scale investigative thriller about a political cover-up builds tension through staged sequences and parallel plot lines in a fairly traditional manner, with dialogue in Korean and Japanese.

short-cuts-2026-programme-03.rationale: The source text is only TIFF's standard mission blurb and says nothing about the films, so the placement defaults to typical Short Cuts patterns: a mix of forms, a few titles with subtitles, and a compilation spanning different tones.

in-conversation-with-lee-min-ho.rationale: An in-person stage interview with Lee Min-ho, a figure central to Korean pop culture worldwide; it screens nothing, sitting nearest to nonfiction discussion rooted in Korean-language cultural background.

children-untold.rationale: Three hours of neorealism set in Tokyo after the war, tracking how conflict robs children of their youth, clear-eyed about kids left behind and mistreated, directed by a major Japanese filmmaker and featuring Koji Yakusho.

brace-your-heart.rationale: A close, many-stranded romance told in Sámi, where the cycles of herding reindeer set the terms of daily life, assembled from tiny gestures and expressive terrain, with abuse and what women bear at its centre

paradise-lost.rationale: Yeon Sang-ho, who made Train to Busan, delivers a tense Korean-language psychological thriller that digs into a mother's grief and, at moments, into genuinely scary territory about trauma and the darker side of people

conversation-with-the-sea.rationale: Jerusalem-set story of mourning and administrative cruelty, 142 min in Arabic and Hebrew, carefully staged, following a guilt-burdened, unheroic protagonist; it works as both critique of society and one man's private search.

ben-imana.rationale: Set in Rwanda's gacaca tribunals, this Kinyarwanda-language film deals with genocide trauma and mothers bearing their rapists' children, building a story across generations; it took the Camera d'Or and runs 131 minutes.

inherit.rationale: A 158-minute Thai occult horror by Banjong Pisanthanakun, who made Pee Mak, keeping the frights polished and effective while running corruption and exploitation through a family drama

coward.rationale: A 155-minute romance between two soldiers in the WWI trenches from Lukas Dhont, whose leads shared the Cannes acting prize; the war's brutality is present but the film stays close, particular and human rather than epic.

bad-lieutenant-tokyo.rationale: Miike drives a lurid, tightly constructed crime saga deep into Tokyo's criminal underside, told in both English and Japanese, with the sensational thrills he is known for

memories-of-a-forest.rationale: A hushed German-language drama set on the land, turning on what gets passed down and what is owed, and Katharina Rabl's first feature builds from terrain and withheld emotion more than from plot events.

turtle-island-rap.rationale: Observational music documentary trailing three Indigenous rappers from grinding for gigs to performing live, keeping a good-humoured, affectionate tone through the rough patches

all-that-she-wants.rationale: Light on its feet, affectionate and contemporary, this romantic comedy delivers on sex and laughs while staying within well-worn crowd-pleasing shapes, its feelings never cutting very deep.

up-against-it.rationale: A sharp-edged comedy that reworks screwball conventions around a daughter's leukemia diagnosis, carried by its name cast in a 152-minute Gala slot.

a-common-story.rationale: A subdued Italian drama about a couple left alone after their daughter moves out, holding on small gestures and stretches of silence; Anna Foglietta's 137-minute first feature, with Alba Rohrwacher

sunburn.rationale: Relaxed, comic teen hangout picture in a Dazed and Confused vein, hot and colour-drenched onscreen, though it moves without much plot and keeps the stakes small.

low-lies-the-land.rationale: A fly-on-the-wall Italian winegrowing documentary, beautifully framed in panoramic widescreen, that builds quiet tension around an offer to sell the land, in the vein of The Truffle Hunters

hope.rationale: Na Hong-jin strings together relentless action sequences, creature-feature spectacle, comedy that swings between terror and laughs, and a final shift into tragedy over 167 minutes in Korean.

josephine.rationale: At 149 minutes, it follows a child after a violent incident, with disciplined, unshowy filmmaking and a camera locked to her point of view that conveys her paranoia instead of reaching for thriller effects.

thirteen-in-gaza.rationale: A close-up coming-of-age story filmed in Gaza, set in a camp where a girl has no security, seclusion or care as she reaches puberty; the treatment stays watchful and weighted, not lurid.

the-city-of-the-living.rationale: Working against true-crime conventions, it handles the social currents around a young man's killing with restraint: a grave Italian drama built on character instead of suspense, though the killing itself supplies genre pull.

we-are-born-good.rationale: A funny, briskly paced comedy-drama about a quarrel that keeps ratcheting up, following Hong Kong characters buried in debt whom grief, rage and fatigue have already ground down

run-terry-run.rationale: A documentary built from archive material about Terry Fox's cross-country run, conventional in form and emotionally weighty because of how his life ended, running 138 minutes in a gala slot.

it-will-happen-tonight.rationale: Nanni Moretti directs a high-spirited romance spanning decades, with a likeable ensemble, warmth and a dry comic touch, told as a straightforward narrative mostly in Italian.

four-seasons-in-java.rationale: Andini's largest-scale work to date, a 167-minute drama centred on a woman confronting sexual violence, mixing fantastical elements with striking imagery and layered metaphor; heavy going and dark.

black-sunflowers.rationale: A patchwork portrait of Ukrainians in their twenties, moving from nightclubs to the front line, its young restless charge and street-racing kicks set beside grief and obligation, made by a director who came from music films.

in-alaska.rationale: An Arctic chase story, tightly wound and grimly funny, follows a young Inuk man branded an eco-terrorist; some dialogue is Inuktitut, the wilderness itself threatens, and mental illness sits at its centre.

ink.rationale: Boyle brings James Graham's play to the screen at speed, tracking how The Sun built its tabloid empire, with a slick, restless visual style and a mean satirical streak.

crystal-lake.rationale: An A24-produced Friday the 13th prequel series that traces Pamela Voorhees through her grief after Jason's drowning while piling up the bodies and delivering gory fun.

what-lies-between-us.rationale: A Danish drama, unsettling and tense, in which mothers face an allegation of sexual assault; its storytelling is straightforward, its rhythm well controlled, its themes hard, its acting forceful.

salvation.rationale: Confident first feature from Scotland following a self-deluding aspiring life coach: a social-realist portrait that is uncomfortable to watch and quietly unsettling, funny in places yet earnest and driven by desperation.

flies.rationale: Shot in black and white with a slow pace and restrained staging, Eimbcke's film follows a solitary woman who builds a family by choice, locating comedy, tenderness and small discoveries in ordinary days.

gentle-monster.rationale: Kreutzer works through heavy subject matter with restraint, building a cold, unsparing family drama centred on sex offences, running 144 minutes in German and arriving as a significant premiere.

long-long-night.rationale: Glowing animated fable pairing a rhino with a penguin, swinging between comedy and deep grief amid poachers and death; a Korean-language first feature in the Centrepiece slot.

i-am-mario.rationale: Sharon Kleinberg's first feature from Mexico follows a trans taxi driver whose unexpected pregnancy backs him into a corner; a restrained, unhurried social drama, with transphobic slurs and graphic sex.

the-beloved.rationale: Sorogoyen's 165-minute film puts an estranged father and daughter together on a location shoot, where manipulation and old injuries resurface; it covers similar ground to Sentimental Value but is harsher and bleaker.

bunker.rationale: A dialogue-heavy Florian Zeller portrait of a marriage strained by wealth, suspicion and career hunger, running 156 minutes, largely in English, carried by Cruz and Bardem and tilting toward thriller unease.

anchors-aweigh.rationale: A first-person essay-film send-up of the Ross McElwee documentary Sherman's March, built from dreamlike sketches whose flat, awkward jokes land in Nathan Fielder territory: alt-comedy that gets big laughs rather than Midnight genre thrills.

ken-russells-the-devils.rationale: Russell's delirious, boundary-breaking film treats the Loudun hysteria, torture and exorcism at once as history, horror film and political allegory, in saturated baroque style with strong body-horror content.

short-cuts-2026-programme-04.rationale: The programmer text is just TIFF's standard institutional mission language and says nothing about the films, so this 130-minute mixed-form shorts collection sits at the default Short Cuts values.

the-black-box-is-orange.rationale: Yuula Benivolski's self-portrait essay work unfolds across ten formally varied sections, using hand-developed 16mm and sound set against image to confront the 1948 Nakba, occupation, and her own implicated recollections.

club-kid.rationale: Jordan Firstman's lively first feature, set in the queer nightlife world, follows a well-worn dramatic-comic shape to a cathartic ending built for audiences, arriving with attention from Cannes and running 152 minutes.

the-lost-children-of-tuam.rationale: A compassionate, weighty drama built from slow record-searching and stubborn follow-through into the deaths of 796 infants, played straight and understated, set in Ireland and in English.

the-violinist.rationale: Animated love story set against WWII Singapore, following its two musicians across eighty years through grief, memory and endurance; runs 144 minutes and took the Cristal, Annecy's top feature award.

bedford-park.rationale: Forceful, unpolished first feature running 151 minutes, moving in English and Korean through inherited trauma and displacement as two people gradually grow close

its-my-time.rationale: A 137-minute Gala comedy in Mandarin and Cantonese starring Michelle Yeoh, built for broad audiences, leaning on tenderness, strong feeling and old regrets inside a familiar rise-to-the-competition structure.

pelechian-project.rationale: Speechless nonfiction built from montage, dense in image and score, moving between exhilaration and grief, each film a bruising tribute to human life and its cycles; radical in form, presented in new restorations.

ha-chan-shake-your-booty.rationale: A Tokyo grief story built as a mannered mix of melodrama and daydream: odd, light-footed, playful, with imagined detours including a giant crow and Dirty Dancing; mostly in Japanese and Spanish, 151 min.

carrie.rationale: Mike Flanagan takes on Stephen King with a direct horror film about school as an engine of shame, escalating toward bloodshed at the prom: amplified genre material, weighty, told in a familiar shape.

american-hostage.rationale: A true-story siege thriller centred on broadcast ethics and the blurred line between reporting an event and becoming part of it, a fairly standard Primetime series whose tension comes from talk and procedure.

the-difficult-bride.rationale: A Bengali-language Centrepiece drama with a body-horror edge, full of vivid visions of catfish, snakes and movement beneath the skin, more concerned with the suffocating demands placed on a bride than with narrative drive.

hombre-al-agua.rationale: A perceptive contemporary manners comedy tracking class and upward mobility, running 146 minutes with a Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking ensemble, built on mood and dry humour more than forward drive

god-bless-you-mr-kopu.rationale: Alex Liu's debut cuts satire against the strut of 1970s hustler and action pictures, accelerating into a fast, tense thriller: a dark comedy played largely in English but rooted in specific Tongan life.

edward-said-between-worlds.rationale: Built from archives, the film lets Said speak for himself, weaving together hundreds of hours of recorded interviews; heavy on Palestine and the Nakba, largely in English with occasional Arabic, running 137 minutes

the-hummingbird-paints-fragrant-songs.rationale: Shot in Spanish and Shipibo, this lyrical, immersive portrait of an artist declines to explain itself, cutting between forest patrols in the Amazon and gallery receptions abroad.

fjord.rationale: Mungiu's Cannes top-prize winner runs 176 minutes as a tightly built, tense trial film turning on a serious ethical question, played in a harsh register with dialogue largely in Romanian and Norwegian.

the-perverts-guide-to-utopias.rationale: Loosely structured essay film that plants \u017di\u017eek inside rebuilt versions of famous movie scenes; dense with ideas and played for impish fun, running 163 minutes.

the-smell-of-apples.rationale: An unsparing Afrikaans-language story of a boy losing his innocence under apartheid, seen from the side that profited, examining how low people can sink; weighty and slow-building, told in a straightforward narrative style

man-in-motion-the-rick-hansen-story.rationale: A standard Gala doc built from interviews and archive footage, honouring Rick Hansen's Man in Motion tour in an uplifting register rather than a grim or formally experimental one.

elephants-in-the-fog.rationale: Abinash Bikram Shah's first feature pairs toughness with gentleness, casting non-professionals and filming the green Nepali landscape in fine detail, as a Kinnar community's old rules press against modern desires.

wavelengths-anoushahpour-aljafari.rationale: A Wavelengths double bill of slow, essayistic nonfiction about recollection and invention: Anoushahpour's portrait of Kurdish villages built around wedding embroideries, and Aljafari's quiet observation of Masao Adachi seeking a passport.

kissed.rationale: Carries the same otherworldly air as Crash and Exotica: a hazy, trance-bound drama about necrophilia that holds the real and the imagined in equilibrium instead of tipping into horror.

everybody-wants-to-fck-me.rationale: Jonathan Schey's first feature is a black comedy skewering self-styled decent men, with real edge in places, escalating absurdly from mild interest into stalking and aggressive chasing, and it withholds any tidy redemption.

the-life-and-deaths-of-wilson-shedd.rationale: An Oklahoma-set drama inside a maximum security prison, 151 minutes tracing an abusive marriage, guilt, and punishment; familiar in shape and weighty in tone, carried by its lead actors.

short-cuts-2026-programme-02.rationale: Note is only TIFF's boilerplate mission statement, so placement rests entirely on the Short Cuts prior: a mixed 131-min shorts block of varied tone and language.

drifter.rationale: Action cinema with an existential streak, swinging between sorrow and thrill: authentic drifting sequences built around a grief-shadowed, soulful character portrait running 177 minutes.

london.rationale: A 150-minute German-language avant-garde road film built from stationary in-car talk, filmed with old-style rear projection, drawing on James Benning, its passengers trading existential talk with the driver.

possible-love.rationale: Lee Chang-dong comes back with a 194-minute work about longing, jealousy, and mourning, building small disclosures of feeling into a quiet study of class and power.

the-julia-set.rationale: A familiar people-first drama tracking a gifted mathematician under contest strain; Niki Byrne's first feature is perceptive and well-acted, but its 142 minutes run on conversation and institutional friction, not momentum.

making-waves-with-hudson-williams.rationale: This is a live discussion with actor Hudson Williams programmed under TIFF Next Wave rather than a screening, so it takes the shape of an on-stage interview and has no film form to speak of.

spirit-guardians-the-last-secret-of-the-.rationale: A three-hour Vietnamese period epic that recalls Kurosawa's historical films, mixing raw physical intensity with lavish ceremony and striking martial arts sequences.

short-cuts-2026-strange-cuts.rationale: The programme note offered nothing specific, so the placement rests on the title Strange Cuts alone, which points to shorts with genre leanings and unconventional form drawn from a range of sources.

the-stunt-driver.rationale: Rowdy but tender comic biopic with the same unruly charge as Goon, built on car stunts and the vulnerability hiding under Ken Carter's swagger.

the-dreamed-adventure.rationale: Grisebach's 194-minute film in Bulgarian, awarded the Jury Prize at Cannes, builds slowly and with great control around diesel smuggling and buried memory, where the crime story is only a small trace of something larger and hazier

bucking-fastard.rationale: Herzog returns to fiction after a long gap with an odd story of sisters who talk as one and love the same man, mixing myth-tinged eccentricity with trial melodrama, in English with name actors.

the-debut.rationale: Jesse Eisenberg draws layered, dark humour out of how gravely community theatre takes itself; a straightforwardly built dramedy carried by its cast, funny and sharp the whole way through.

the-spiral.rationale: Paolo Strippoli's four-part Italian-language psychological horror about a bargain with a devilish stranger, gorgeously shot and steeped in dread, tightening its grip across 145 minutes

dorothy.rationale: Karthik Subbaraj's three-hour Tamil film moves between noir, gangster picture, romance, Bruce Lee-style fight staging and Hawks-like slapstick, against a backdrop of routine brutality and patriarchal power in rural Tamil Nadu.

mr-nelson-did-you-kill-people.rationale: Tsukamoto's war picture drives forward without letup in a raw, physical visual style, an unsparing and brutal study of trauma carrying graphic violence and strobe effects, running 146 minutes largely in English.

like-magic.rationale: A first-person documentary essay that pieces together large amounts of found footage and witness accounts of Cali's cartel-years bloodshed, moving at a contemplative, weighted pace instead of a driving one

ten-dark-women.rationale: Kon Ichikawa's chic, mocking rework of noir and melodrama, with jazz scoring, exact framing, and dry wit, now in a 4K restoration: an old film revived by turning genre conventions into bleak comedy.

the-only-living-pickpocket-in-new-york.rationale: A quiet crime story that doubles as a reflection on a shifting era, made in the character-focused style of 1970s New Hollywood, with Turturro's appeal holding it together.

vintage-violence.rationale: An internet-saturated crime romp in the vein of Japanese V-Cinema, built from layered device screens, with brawling excess and inventive chases across Tokyo: quick, comic, heavily stylized genre work.

wavelengths-3-time-and-tide.rationale: A Wavelengths short-film selection spanning 65mm formal experiment, Baroque trompe l'oeil, salvaged 8mm footage of Roma migration, and an essay drawing on Duras and Conrad: openly avant-garde, meditative work.

being-heumann.rationale: A 157-minute audience-friendly biopic of disability activism directed by Siân Heder after CODA, told in a familiar shape and carrying emotional weight comparable to her earlier film, driven by the pace of a building takeover campaign.

wild-horse-nine.rationale: A Martin McDonagh dark comedy set on Easter Island, running 148 minutes, following two odd CIA operatives through mounting suspicion and a hard look back, carried by his sharp trademark dialogue.

tender-loving-care.rationale: A perceptive Mike Leigh study of everyday people facing age and family duty, moving but not sappy, honest but not bleak, and often funny.

after-elena.rationale: A Spanish-language drama about a family after a death that stays soft-edged and refuses to judge or turn maudlin, drawing its weight from tiny gestures, comic absurdity and melancholy.

love-of-your-life.rationale: Wide-ranging romantic study of one woman's love and grief, moving between tender, sorrowful, and clear-eyed registers, told conventionally across several years and countries in English at 136 minutes

rescue.rationale: Observational documentary on Mediterranean rescue that begins with a violent kidnapping at sea and unfolds with such tension that its non-fiction status is easy to forget; largely in Arabic, with phone video smuggled out of captivity.

everest-the-other-side.rationale: Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi shot for IMAX: a grand, feeling-heavy record of a lethal ski descent off Everest, pitched like Free Solo but running longer and weighing more

slow-horses.rationale: Episodes of a spy series that keeps up its driving pace and grim comedy, with sharp writing that makes the unglamorous business of espionage consistently fun to watch

alpha-gang.rationale: David and Nathan Zellner's dry sci-fi comedy, in which invaders dressed as 1950s bikers lose their mission to closeness, music, grief and beauty, playing its jokes oddly and fielding a well-known ensemble

in-conversation-with-chris-rock.rationale: An in-person stage conversation with Chris Rock covering the many sides of his working life, presented as a comedy-inflected nonfiction event rather than a film with a story

in-conversation-with-rachel-morrison.rationale: An in-person stage discussion with Rachel Morrison, nominated for an Oscar as a cinematographer and now directing, tracing her career path: nonfiction talk rather than a screening, centred on craft, not on drama or genre.

the-face-of-horror.rationale: Anna Biller shoots on 35mm to imitate lurid Technicolor horror, running 150 minutes of arch, bloody genre play whose dry humour sits atop melodrama played straight, mannered in style rather than driven by pace

babies.rationale: A crowd-pleasing ensemble comedy with a big cast, weighing the choice of parenthood; warm, familiar in shape, funny and down-to-earth without much riding on it.

glaxo.rationale: Benjamin Naishtat's Argentinian revenge story moves across three timelines, building tension slowly, thick with period atmosphere, and looking hard and without softening at the country's history of violence.

rapinoe.rationale: Rather than a standard tribute film, this athlete portrait went to Rebeca Huntt of Beba, who brings a daring, unconventional approach: light on its feet, inward-looking, and attentive to the family forces that shaped Rapinoe.

congo-boy.rationale: Shot with a restless handheld camera and cut to the beat of the hero's rapping, this Sango, French and Lingala film follows a scrambling teenage refugee through hard circumstances with warmth and lift rather than despair

clarissa.rationale: The Esiri brothers move Woolf's Mrs. Dalloway to present-day Nigeria, 164 minutes shot on 35mm inside its characters' heads, holding time still for reflection and existential reckoning while Boko Haram combat trauma and PTSD run underneath

redefined-short-film-showcase.rationale: A set of five shorts by Indigenous and Canadian directors working in a first-person mode, taking up questions of heritage, identity, where one belongs and sovereignty, with a form that leans essayistic and documentary.

short-cuts-2026-programme-06.rationale: Note is boilerplate mission statement with no film detail; placed at neutral defaults for a mixed Short Cuts anthology programme, which tends toward mild formal play and varied language.

all-about-corinne.rationale: A tasty French showbiz comedy that folds in on itself, casting Huppert as a lifelong background actor while real stars appear as themselves; lively, engrossing, and full of jokes only insiders would catch, running 145 minutes.

life-of-jorge-luis-borges.rationale: Running 370 minutes in Wavelengths, Llinas, who made La Flor, builds an essay film that keeps fact and fabrication indistinguishable: learned, wandering, full of play, and asking a great deal of its audience

bleeding-hearts.rationale: Shot in monochrome with old lenses, Andrew Morgan follows an alt-country trio through love and professional friction, watching rather than narrating, unflinching about the mess without turning grim

ah-girl.rationale: Ang's own childhood feeds this drama set in 1990s Singapore, where gentle camerawork, everyday texture and blurred dream passages carry a girl through her parents' split with a sweet-sour sense of already-lived memory.

the-man-i-love.rationale: A naturalistic look at artists during the AIDS years, dwelling on unplanned turns, talk over meals, and extended theatre rehearsals, its warmth shadowed throughout by the illness.

obsession.rationale: A first feature blending horror and comedy around a Monkey's Paw wish, dryly funny and nerve-tightening in the vein of Barbarian, running a substantial 138 minutes.

djinn-wedding.rationale: Ferit Karahan's mood-driven family story tracks four siblings across childhood, youth and adulthood over 162 minutes, built around an extended wedding sequence, withholding enough to stay enigmatic while patriarchy and old memories press in

everytime.rationale: A mourning family drifts through something like a fever dream, lensed by Aftersun cinematographer Gregory Oke, directed by Un Certain Regard winner Sandra Wollner; 149 unhurried minutes built to stay with you afterwards.

everything-else-is-noise.rationale: Wavelengths hosts Pereda's wry, self-aware social comedy of small disasters, built as a chamber piece with pared-down means and a Lubitsch-like lightness, running 101 minutes in Spanish

tangles.rationale: Leah Nelson adapts Sarah Leavitt's Alzheimer's memoir in hand-drawn 2D animation, an emotionally weighty story lightened by a voice cast stacked with comedians

wild-wild-east.rationale: Part western, part wartime noir, Jan Holoubek's tense film unfolds in occupied Poland in 1943, tracing greed and treachery among shell-shocked villagers and Nazi officials; 135 minutes, in Polish, German and Ukrainian.

ladies-and-gentlemen-brian-mulroney.rationale: A hallucinatory montage built from archives, blending satire and collage in the vein of Adam Curtis fed too many Heritage Minutes, largely English with French passages.

musk.rationale: Running 260 minutes, this is the largest-scale film Gibney has attempted, built around a novel graphics-driven visual approach, and it asks a lot of viewers as an English-language investigative haul

alice.rationale: A large-scale French-language costume drama about Alice Guy-Blache in Belle Epoque Paris, starring Berenice Bejo, told in a familiar prestige-biopic mode.

the-fortunate-isles.rationale: Held-back epic about the remorse of conquest, shot with a hands-on camera and an ominous look all its own: a measured, poetic, formally heightened period piece on bondage and water scarcity, in Spanish and Arabic.

julian.rationale: A Cartoon Saloon animation for families, its expressive drawing carrying wit and warmth, light in touch instead of weighty, spoken largely in English with occasional Spanish.

the-ultra-runner.rationale: Gripping camerawork from a race across the Arctic combines with polished, well-staged reconstructions of a childhood in Romania and years behind bars, yielding a driving endurance documentary carrying some subtitles.

the-betrayers.rationale: Absorbing, polished adaptation of a novel: a moral and political drama set in Yalta, mostly in English yet saturated in Soviet-Israeli history, driven by talk and character instead of momentum.

ashes.rationale: An immigrant story in Spanish and Catalan about being uprooted repeatedly and enduring the hardest ordeals, handled with adult restraint and shading, told in familiar form and weighted with emotional cost

la-gradiva.rationale: Running 175 minutes, this French-Italian ensemble film about young people growing up, set in Pompeii, pairs lyrical imagery with serious ideas and a shooting style close to documentary.

the-housewife.rationale: Set in 1964, Ben Shirinian's debut works as a mind-and-history drama about complicity with Nazism, moving from taut thriller into the courtroom, told in a smooth, familiar style despite the weight of its subject.

elsinore.rationale: A biographical drama set during the AIDS crisis, following Ian Charleson as he takes on Hamlet, played by Andrew Scott at the peak of his work, and pitched as physically immediate and emotionally heavy while still warm and funny

i-play-rocky.rationale: Peter Farrelly, of Green Book, delivers a mainstream, audience-friendly biopic full of grit and heart; at 157 minutes it still keeps momentum as an underdog-makes-good story.

lautre.rationale: Alexandre Franchi's black-humoured thriller keeps a man's endangered mind and body inside one hospital room, running on medicated unreality, physical immediacy, stretches of dread, and restless nerve.

rogue-trooper.rationale: Military science fiction from the 2000 AD strip, made with performance capture, heavy on graphic violence and lurid visual excess, though Jones holds onto the source's mischievous, absurd British satire through Berry, Clement, and Morgan.

look-back.rationale: Hirokazu Kore-eda films Tatsuki Fujimoto's manga on 35mm in live action, tracking two young artists through a full year of seasons with strong feeling, gentleness, and sorrow at how short a life is.

krux.rationale: Set in a village during WWII, Tony Vahl's 122-minute German-language first feature tracks ethical breakdown and mass panic through striking camerawork, and does not flinch from historical brutality.

girl-group.rationale: A broadly appealing music comedy stacked with comic performers and a strong song selection, running a familiar redemption path as a washed-up pop singer mentors aspiring young performers.

muyi.rationale: A French-language animated fable about growing up, set in China, whose appeal rests on inventive design and playful figures such as a tiger that eats no meat and a guide with magic.

the-age-of-goodbyes.rationale: Long thought impossible to adapt, this 172-minute metafiction braids timelines that demand effort from the viewer, with striking images and layers that open up on a second pass.

gail.rationale: An offbeat music documentary built around one person, trailing a fan whose unwavering worship produces some uncomfortable encounters; its tone is affectionate and dryly funny, a little odd, never weighty or heavily styled.

on-behalf-of-my-son.rationale: A 178-minute Brazilian drama on culpability and mourning, held at a quiet, controlled pitch, in which a mother travels to ask the bereaved families for forgiveness.

double-freedom.rationale: In Wavelengths, Alonso answers his own La libertad with an unhurried 35mm portrait of daily labour, cast with non-actors, that turns away from conventional storytelling and thinks patiently about caretaking and what freedom means.

ancestors.rationale: A hypnotic drift through 1980s London rendered like a half-remembered dream, where recollection and yearning blur; a slow, vision-filled lament for what the AIDS years left behind, sorrowful yet never sinking into hopelessness.

marie-madeleine.rationale: Gessica Geneus retells the Mary Magdalene story in Jacmel, Haiti, with surreal flourishes, deep saturated colour and Jacmel's noise functioning as a character; sensual and celebratory, though shadowed by evangelical repression and violence

the-idiots.rationale: A costume-drama account of Dostoevsky's compulsive gambling and of Anna, his wife, two people given over to art while their relationship stays turbulent; standard awards-season filmmaking, 148 minutes, mostly English-language.

the-surgeon.rationale: Michelle Yeoh anchors a fast, brutal action picture built on tight fight choreography, surgical gore and well-chosen rock cuts, working squarely inside blockbuster genre form.

villeneuve-the-rise-of-a-legend.rationale: A high-octane life story of Gilles Villeneuve, following a familiar arc of ascent and early death, told in French with plenty of on-track spectacle.

arne-goes-to-space.rationale: A quietly funny, tender oddity from rural Sweden: two aging brothers take in a small extraterrestrial whose ship crashes nearby, played straight and unhurried, with one brother's failing health running underneath.

toy-gun-bandit.rationale: A high-octane crime comedy from Quebec whose chaos keeps mounting, driven by jittery, heedless momentum and offset by real tenderness plus a storyline about a young addict sliding downward.

evil-genius.rationale: A dramatized true-crime case staged with the sly comic menace of a Coen Brothers picture, full of killings and double-crosses, carried by a Gala-scale cast and a plot that doubles back in time.

phoolan.rationale: A tense, absorbing 143-minute Hindi thriller staged around a two-day standoff, carrying Mehta's understated documentary-style approach to true crime, and dealing directly with caste oppression and sexual violence.

your-mother-your-mother-your-mother.rationale: A boldly imaginative action thriller set in Texas, packed with spectacle, suspense, tenderness and bloodshed, starring Mahershala Ali as a contract killer who refuses to use firearms.

viva-carmen.rationale: A French hand-painted take on Carmen, seen from the perspective of children, with loose painterly gestures onscreen while the gravity of Bizet's tragedy holds firm against the story's brutality.

the-road-not-taken.rationale: A slick, high-feeling domestic drama on early-onset Alzheimer's, 165 minutes in Chinese: close-focus character work with mainstream reach, and only mild disorientation at the level of form.

the-remotes.rationale: A 183-minute Wavelengths entry in Tagalog that runs long and skips between scenes, mixing science fiction, noir and detective work with trance-like nocturnal driving and the sorrow left by colonial history.

2-6-seconds-death-in-the-outback.rationale: A tense four-part documentary series (first two episodes, 148 min) that pieces together a police killing, including body-camera images, sitting beside true crime without adopting its habits; shared mourning, some Warlpiri spoken.

the-liberation.rationale: Cult coercion and mourning treated with wrenching force across 154 minutes, built on its actors, carrying a creeping thriller-like threat while keeping to conventional filmmaking shape

idda.rationale: Slow, enigmatic study of two women whose strained bond surfaces during an ascent of Etna, with quiet menace, an unforeseen bereavement, and roaming, ominous camerawork; in Italian.

growth-of-the-soil.rationale: Running 185 minutes, this straightforwardly told period epic follows the hardships of carving out a farm in northern Norway, staged in a strictly realist register and performed with weight and restraint.

misty-green.rationale: Chris Rock skewers racism in the film business with jokes that cut, while the story carries real weight: a looming eviction, a brother in a bipolar crisis, and an ugly proposition attached to a lot of money.

lemonade.rationale: Kim Bartley's first fiction feature follows a young man aging out of Irish foster care, watching him closely for humour, affection and small everyday pleasures instead of bleakness, with Barry Keoghan steadying the film.

nosotros.rationale: Joaquin Ruano's first feature works in a subdued, precise register, following a rural Guatemalan man who moves to the city for work and finds a tender, precarious love with a trans woman while hostility presses in.

closing-night.rationale: Sharp, funny family conflict built on cutting exchanges that eventually softens into something tender; a standard talk-based ensemble picture, 145 minutes, in English.

future-tense.rationale: Jenna Cato Bass directs a time-travel science fiction picture, spoken partly in Xhosa and Afrikaans, that binds a love story to fears of climate breakdown and the brutality of the colonial era.

zjili-a-story-of-sisterhood-and-the-burd.rationale: A Ghanaian social-realist film about kayayei head porters, handled plainly rather than for shock value, running 149 minutes in Dagbani and Twi, built on research and dedicated to a woman killed by a load she was carrying.

short-cuts-2026-programme-05.rationale: Note is boilerplate mission text with no film detail; placements default to Short Cuts shorts-programme averages of mixed tone and moderate formal play.

a-talent-for-murder.rationale: A slow-burning, enclosed thriller built on two people sparring in words, with sharp reversals and cutting talk, funny and malicious rather than action-driven, in English, drawn from a play.

tenzing.rationale: A 158-minute, formally traditional biopic of Tenzing Norgay, handsomely shot and uplifting in tone, with the stakes of a survival adventure but nothing experimental in its construction

trees-are-watching.rationale: Bahman Ghobadi, a leading Kurdish-Iranian director, mixes mind-unsettling horror with regional folklore through dreamlike sequences of intense hallucinatory style and gory theatrical excess, performed mostly in Kurdish and Turkish.

wavelengths-2-this-suffocating-now.rationale: A Wavelengths shorts set built on essayistic work and camera-made effects: Tafakory's clear, multi-strand history, Kosugi's poetic 8mm, a walk shot on night vision, and a blunt, physical political charge

masc.rationale: Bertil Nilsson's first feature, filmed across a year in five parts, watches a young gay neurodivergent man adjust himself across London settings, avoiding crisis or coming-out beats, and closing on a wordless surprise.

faith.rationale: A work of British social realism about grief carried at full force, made with disciplined precision and a naturalistic surface, its pull emotional and withholding rather than driven by momentum.

neil-peart-no-ones-disciple.rationale: A standard-issue music documentary built around thrilling live playing and a mood tilted toward celebration rather than sorrow, even while it takes in Peart's bereavement and his own death.

purgatory.rationale: Set in the 1980s, a warm and lightly comic growing-up story that sits alongside Lady Bird and Eighth Grade, told in familiar form and running 134 minutes

a-girl-unknown.rationale: Told in chapters over 158 minutes and in Chinese, it follows a girl through abandonment and repeated uprooting, played with held-back performances, subdued and sore but not without hope.

union-town.rationale: Energizing observational documentary from twice Oscar-honoured Barbara Kopple, braiding three New York union drives across several years; standard form, partly in Spanish, 136 minutes

the-world-before.rationale: A hushed adolescence story on a Korean island, its camera mostly fixed and watchful, drawing incident from ordinary life over 145 tender, faintly sorrowful minutes.

prima-facie.rationale: A sharp courtroom picture in which a defence lawyer ends up on the other side of the case, wrenching and forceful, working within a familiar leading-actor legal-drama mode

atonement.rationale: A Gala-slot drama built around its cast, drawing on true events to trace wartime guilt and the search for reconciliation; 148 minutes, traditional in construction, partly in Arabic.

magazine.rationale: A dialogue-driven, watchful first feature following a young poet interning in the literary world before #MeToo; the storytelling is traditional and the social observation sharp, running a fairly long 135 minutes.

always-lalisa.rationale: A polished, access-driven portrait of a pop star built from standout stage footage and backstage material, conventional in shape, partly in Thai and Korean, and offered above all as a payoff for devoted followers.

head-to-head.rationale: A Persian-language nested production whose comedy takes aim at how male filmmakers depict women and at state censorship, its ridicule sharpening as the political stakes grow heavier.

la-bola-negra.rationale: Running 185 minutes, this three-part drama draws on Lorca to trace gay lives silenced by fascism, its strands drawing together on a grand, opera-like scale, shadowed by the writer's killing, and fronted by well-known actors.

report-to-mother.rationale: Blending fictional narrative with documentary observation, including verite footage of labour struggles, this Malayalam political film was shot in black and white using only available light and appears here in a 4K restoration.

the-diary-of-a-chambermaid.rationale: Placed in Wavelengths as Jude's broadly comic attack on present-day servitude: a French/Romanian satire heavy on dialogue and formal risk, yet warmer toward its heroine than expected.

light-pillar.rationale: A sad, boldly designed film about loneliness that draws the waking world by hand and shoots the VR world live, unhurried and rueful, taking real formal risks while pulling you in gently.

yaga.rationale: A coastal-town investigation shaded by the Baba Yaga legend, mixing scares with mystery-solving, dry back-and-forth between its leads, and a persistent sense that something inhuman waits just out of sight

short-cuts-2026-programme-01.rationale: The source text is only TIFF's generic organizational blurb and says nothing about the films, so the slot rests on standard Short Cuts expectations: a varied shorts block with some experimental technique and entries from abroad.

iron-boy.rationale: An autobiographical coming-of-age tale in French, animated in hand-painted images by a director who once worked at Pixar, lovely and playful in tone, and honoured by a special jury award at Cannes

neverman.rationale: A trans elder losing her memory to Alzheimer's is kept in a chilly, forbidding care facility, her past surfacing in flashback; the result is a weighty, mostly familiar drama with a slight undercurrent of menace.

whatcha-want.rationale: Mina Shum handles class and gender lightly in this audience-friendly story of a wealthy wife trapped in luxury who returns to dancing, drawing on Crazy Rich Asians and Flashdance, partly in Cantonese and Mandarin

happily-ever-after.rationale: A Mandarin-language family drama following two sisters, told in a conventional style, holding comedy and emotional strain in even measure, and easy for audiences to enter.

sisters.rationale: A Spanish and Basque family drama about an assault within the family and the court case that follows, watchful in method and quietly grieving in tone, slow and weighty, subtitled, told in a familiar shape.

wavelengths-1-house-and-home.rationale: A Wavelengths shorts set of sensory, poem-like essay works about dwelling and remembrance, ranging from archive-based reflection to a calmly furious account of housing and exploitation.

the-final-act.rationale: Sophie Deraspe, who has twice taken TIFF's Best Canadian Feature prize, pairs philosophical enquiry into dying with the final days of people choosing assisted death, grave in subject yet full of warmth, beauty, and lightness.

woman-unknown.rationale: Set in Copenhagen just after the occupation, a tightening thriller about fear and crowd vengeance, told in a conventional register in Danish across 156 minutes, with some scenes hard to watch

below.rationale: A Newfoundland family story crossed with something monstrous in the water, told in familiar creature-feature shape, holding domestic warmth against cold sea horror.

bas-book.rationale: Ashley Duong stages her father's memoir as a film-within-a-film, its pace unhurried and contemplative rather than driving, mostly in Vietnamese, with relatives restaging their own past as the structure for its formal experiment
